cases.case_text: 37-year-old man with muscle twitching off and on for the last year.  He will develop twitching of the calves.  It is visible and is a rippling under the skin.  At times it involves the eyelids, biceps, and chest.  Tends to be worse with exercise but can happen at other times.  Has also had difficulty with cramping in his calves and feet at night.  It is intermittent and will usually last for a minute or 2 but can occur several times a day.  The twitching and cramps wax and wane.  One year ago it was occurring daily but then disappeared and has now come back over the last 3 months.  He also develops intermittent tingling on any part of his body typically around the time of the cramps. Denies any weakness, dysarthria, dysphagia, or weight loss.  Past history of hypertension and depression.  Currently on atorvastatin 40 mg daily and Lexapro 20 mg daily.  Neurologic exam is normal.  What are the next steps?
rubric: If EMG normal no further work up

cases.case_text: 68-year-old man with a history of Parkinson's disease for the last 10 years.  Symptoms started with a right hand rest tremor and soft voice.  He has been treated with carbidopa/levodopa since.  Has gradually developed increasing bradykinesia in his right arm as well as mild difficulty swallowing along with dysarthria.  His gait is slower.  For the last 5 years has difficulty with motor fluctuations.  Has gradually increased his carbidopa/levodopa dose to 25/100 2 pills every 3 hours while awake accompanied by entacapone 200 mg with each levodopa dose.  He has an increasing ability to move beginning 30 minutes after each dose but develops dyskinesias for an hour to an hour and a half after each dose which can sometimes be debilitating.  He then has wearing off with freezing of his gait and recently had a few falls.  Tried amantadine without benefit.  On examination he took his medications 60 minutes prior to exam.  His voice is still soft but he has significant head, trunk, and arm dyskinesias with normal tone and his gait is inhibited by dyskinesias.  What are the next steps?

71-year-old man is seen in the office with a history of diabetes, lumbar laminectomy 7 years ago and chronic back pain who is on metformin, atorvastatin, and lisinopril.  He typically takes Flexeril as needed and about 2 months ago his low back pain worsened.  He had a Medrol Dosepak which gave him slight relief.  Then had an epidural steroid injection which gave him partial relief but over the last 7 days his back pain has returned.  He has noticed weakness in his right leg and is stumbling a bit.  He has also been fatigued more than usual.  On examination temperature is 99.4, blood pressure 150/92, pulse 96, respirations 16.  He has tenderness in the low back.  Straight leg raising is negative.  Right hip flexion and ankle dorsiflexion are 4/5.  Left leg strength is 5/5.  He has reduced pinprick and vibratory sense in the feet.  DTRs are 2+ in the arms 3+ at the knees and absent at the ankles with neutral toes.  His gait is antalgic.  What are the next steps?
rubric: Leg weakness and knee hyperreflexia are concerning for myelopathy
Concern over epidural abscess given fatigue and mild elevation of temperature
Needs admission and MRI of the thoracic and lumbar spine
